script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this flow is inferred only from L3 form and the defensive splits, not from a book score. MIN can lean on Aaron Jones (52 carries, 203 rush yards over 3 games) into a MIA run defense allowing 3.82 YPC, and MIA blitzes only 32%, so MIN's QB (EPA -0.22 vs blitz, +0.02 with no blitz) mostly avoids his bad blitz sample. MIA is the pressured offense: MIN blitzes 73% and the MIA QB is -0.26 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=31) versus +0.06 with no blitz, while MIN holds the run at 3.52 YPC with only 8 runs of 10+. Base case is MIN on schedule in the run game, MIA in long downs, deep air yards stalling, and a lower-event MIA skill game rather than a shootout.
script.flip1: The 73% blitz backfires: Malik Willis (17 carries, 101 rush yards, 5.94 YPC over L3) scrambles and MIA throws quick into the middle, where MIN allows 10.04 YPA, so Dulcich, Achane and Washington short production rises and MIN cannot just hand the ball to Jones.
script.flip2: MIA scores first anyway and MIN trails, Jones's 17.3 carries per game get cut, and dropbacks rise for Jefferson (18 targets, 179 rec yards) and Addison (16 targets, 221 air yards) against MIA's leaky secondary (middle 10.57 YPA, 9 passes of 20+ on 76 attempts), while MIA's own deep shots still mostly fail under pressure.

matchup.shell: MISSING: coverage charting. No MOFO/MOFC split and no man-vs-zone rate, so no shell is assigned. Location splits only: MIN allows 7.11 YPA left (37 att), 10.04 middle (28 att), 5.25 right (48 att). MIA allows 8.62 left (26 att), 10.57 middle (23 att), 8.37 right (27 att).
matchup.pressure: MIN blitz rate 73% against a MIA QB at -0.26 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=31) and +0.06 with no blitz. That is the main pressure edge: it should cut deep WR yards and only theoretically lift TE/RB checkdowns, because the negative blitz EPA says drives may die before those catches become yards. MIA blitzes only 32%; MIN QB is -0.22 EPA vs blitz (n=40) and +0.02 with no blitz, so MIN mostly faces the less-bad look.
matchup.bleeds: MIN bleeds the middle (10.04 YPA), is sound to the right (5.25), and is firm on the ground (3.52 YPC, 8 runs of 10+, 12 passes of 20+ on 127 attempts). MIA bleeds the middle worse (10.57 YPA) and is soft outside (left 8.62, right 8.37), with 3.82 YPC allowed, 9 runs of 10+, and 9 passes of 20+ on only 76 attempts.
matchup.overlap: MIA's top target is Malik Washington (23 targets, 152 rec yards, 275 air yards), a high-air profile into a 73% blitz, which is a negative overlap for deep yards. The positive MIA overlap is short/middle: Dulcich (12 targets, 90 rec yards, 68 air yards) into MIN's 10.04 middle YPA. MIN's cleaner overlap is Jefferson (18 targets, 179 yards, 189 air) and Addison (16 targets, 111 yards, 221 air) into a secondary that leaks on every side, especially the middle. Jones's carry load meets only a moderate 3.82 YPC run defense, not a bleed.

form: Last-3-games roles only, no season averages. Jones is a stable lead back: 52 carries, 203 rush yards (67.7 per game, 3.90 YPC) and just 7 targets, 34 rec yards, -7 air yards (11.3 rec yards per game). Mason is the change-up (15/59). MIA's backfield is Achane-led (34/127 plus 12 targets and 49 rec yards); Gordon is the inefficient second back (20/48, 2.4 YPC) and does not appear in the target table. Willis's 17/101 rushing (5.94 YPC) is efficiency MIN's 3.52 YPC allowed should pressure. Washington is the usage king at 23 targets and 50.7 rec yards per game but on 275 air yards. Bell is the deep specialist: 10 targets, 92 rec yards, 180 air yards (about 18 air yards per target), 30.7 rec yards per game. Dulcich is steady at the number: 12 targets, 90 yards, 68 air, 30.0 per game. Addison's 111 yards on 221 air yards and Miller's 92 yards on 4 targets look fluky relative to opportunity. Hockenson is 13 targets and 76 yards (25.3 per game). No similar-defense or per-game splits are in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both unders lost. Jones cleared 19.5 because MIN fell behind, a flip that cannot be priced with the spread missing, and the staff answered MIA's 10.57 middle YPA with screens, turning 2.3 targets a game into one 25-yard dump-off night; 19.5 is only a single screen above a three-game total of 34 yards, and there are no game splits to prove that night has not already happened once. Gordon cleared 34.5 because Achane did not keep the 34-carry lead share, which this pack cannot rule out with the injury report missing, and Gordon's 6.7 carries jumped into the teens against a front that has already allowed 8 runs of 10+, or he was suddenly targeted on blitz checkdowns the target table does not show. That Achane-absence case is the real hole in the Gordon leg, which is why it stays a lean and not a strong play; it is not dropped only because the pack still lists Achane as the lead back and contains no news that the role flipped.
slip_story: One script only: MIN runs through a moderate MIA front and does not need Jones in the pass game, while MIA cannot sustain a ground game into a 73% blitz and a 3.52 YPC run defense, so the secondary back stays capped. Jones recyds under and Gordon rushrecyds under win together in that base script and still fit the blitz-backfires flip, because MIA's extra quick game would go to Washington, Dulcich and Achane rather than to Gordon's carries, and Jones still is not a MIN target. They do not belong with a shootout stack, MIA skill overs, a Willis rush over, or a total over. No TD legs and one market per player. A third leg was not forced: Addison under 62.5 fights MIA's leaky secondary and his own 221 air yards, and Washington under 40.5 fights a 50.7-yard L3.
